angles: The skills marketplace ecosystem is fragmented across SkillsMP (2.1M skills), Skills.sh (Vercel's package manager), and GitHub — each serves a different discovery model
Skills are the cross-platform 'write once, run anywhere' standard for agent extensibility — not plugins, not vendor lock-in
Progressive disclosure architecture is the key innovation: skills add only 50-100 tokens until needed, keeping context windows lean
The Agentic AI Foundation (Linux Foundation) signals industry standardization around AGENTS.md and MCP as open infrastructure
Each major agent has a different skills strategy: Claude Code (hooks + subagents + skills), Codex CLI (Goal mode + skills.sh), Cursor (cloud agents + skills), Gemini/Antigravity (MCP + skills)
Enterprise adoption of skills is driven by codifying tribal knowledge — deployment standards, security policies, code review checklists as portable skill packages
The Ralph Wiggum loop technique enables autonomous multi-hour execution by having agents self-iterate until completion criteria are met
outline: Introduction: why agent skills marketplaces became essential in 2026
What are Agent Skills? The SKILL.md format and progressive disclosure architecture
The three major skills marketplaces: SkillsMP (2.1M skills), Skills.sh by Vercel (package manager), and GitHub (community repos)
Skills.sh deep dive: npx skills add, leaderboard, cross-platform compatibility with 35+ agents
SkillsMP deep dive: 2.1M catalog, SOC occupation taxonomy, REST API
Claude Code's skills ecosystem: hooks, subagents, and the plugin marketplace
Codex CLI skills: Goal mode integration, skills.sh support, Ralph Wiggum autonomous loop
Cursor Agent skills: cloud-VM background agents with parallel fan-out
Gemini CLI to Antigravity CLI transition: what happens to skills on June 18, 2026
The Agentic AI Foundation: AGENTS.md and MCP as open infrastructure standards
Enterprise adoption: codifying tribal knowledge as portable skill packages
How to choose a skills marketplace: discovery, installation, governance, and cross-platform portability
Conclusion: skills are the 'write once, run anywhere' layer for agentic coding in 2026
